mutant.description: The load-bearing assertion of the whole seam is ONE dict entry: a producer that FAILED maps to INSTRUMENT_FAILED. Arm M rewrites exactly that -- '"FAILED": "INSTRUMENT_FAILED"' -> '"FAILED": "OK"' -- in a COPY of estate_report_runner.py (never the real file) and feeds the mutated consumer the same genuinely-failed artifact R1 produced. The anchor's uniqueness in the source is asserted BEFORE mutating, so the arm REFUSES rather than silently mutating nothing (W2-S17, and the same refusal OS-s-10's battery hit when OS-s-14 re-pointed its anchor).
mutant.expected: If the red arms are real, the mutated consumer must read a FAILED artifact as status OK -- the silent-seam shape W2-S21 found, where a broken instrument and a clean answer become byte-identical to the reader. If it still read INSTRUMENT_FAILED, R2 and R3 would be passing for some reason other than the mapping they claim to test, and this battery's red arms would be decoration.
mutant.observed: Mutated FAILED->OK; the consumer then read the genuinely-failed artifact as status=OK. The arm PASSES BY DETECTING that, which is what makes R2, R3 and R8 real rather than assumed. Separately, R8 is itself a discrimination control on the RENDERING axis: holding the consumer fixed and changing only the artifact flips 4151 rendered bytes containing no failure marker to 1436 bytes containing 'PRODUCED NO DATA', so a working seam and a silent one are not byte-identical to the reader.

determinism.method: Same-input repeat, twice, in-session, at the AMENDED path: the O18-AC1 invocation exactly as the face names it, rc captured unpiped on each, and the VERDICT SET (arm name plus PASS/FAIL/NOT-EVALUATED, extracted with an anchored regex) diffed between the two runs. The verdict set rather than the whole stdout is the right comparand here and the reason is stated: the battery stamps a UTC timestamp and mkdtemp paths into its own output by construction, so a byte-hash of stdout would differ on every run and would test the clock rather than the arms.
